results.summary: This design is a SPI-configurable watchdog timer intended to supervise an external microcontroller. The host sets a timeout over SPI and periodically kicks the watchdog either by SPI write or by a rising edge on a dedicated pin; if kicks stop, the watchdog first raises an IRQ warning and then pulls an active-low reset line low. It supports eight timeouts from 5.24 ms to 5.37 s with an optional prescaler, a window mode that flags kicks arriving too early, a lock bit that freezes configuration, and fault flags that survive the reset pulse so the cause can be read back. The design is notable for its two-stage response, giving the host a grace period to cancel a reset, and for its window mode that catches firmware stuck in a loop kicking too fast.

This project implements a simple game that outputs a VGA video signal and uses a gamepad for input. It renders graphics on a VGA display and includes game logic for player interaction. The design is notable for its use of a gamepad interface and VGA output, making it a complete interactive gaming experience. It is intended for educational or recreational purposes.

This project implements the measurement-update step of a basic Kalman filter as a fixed-function hardware accelerator in a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It performs matrix operations and includes a register file for storing state and covariance values. The design is intended for digital signal processing applications and is notable for its fixed-point arithmetic and FSM-based control. It is verified with a cocotb testbench.

This project implements a perceptron-based neural network classifier. It uses bit-serial processing and includes a 7-segment display for output. The design is notable for its esoteric approach to neural network implementation and its use of a UART interface for communication. It is intended for machine learning inference tasks.

This project implements Conway's Game of Life as a cellular automaton. It outputs a VGA video signal and renders graphics on a display. The design is notable for its real-time simulation and visual output. It is intended for educational or recreational purposes.

This project is a temperature sensor design that uses an analog oscillator to generate a frequency proportional to temperature. It includes a sensor interface and is intended for educational purposes. The design is notable for its simplicity and analog approach. It is suitable for temperature measurement applications.
